newsitem.title: UK: Bosnia peace process review conference opens.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia peace process review conference opens.

text.p: A major conference opened in London on Wednesday to review the year-old Bosnian peace process.

The conference is expected to criticise the country's various ethnic communities for not sticking to the terms of the Dayton peace agreement which ended the 43-month war in the former Yugoslav republic.
The two-day Peace Implementation Conference is being attended by more than 50 national delegations as well as representatives from major aid agencies.
Delegates will discuss ways of rebuilding the ravaged country one year after the Dayton deal was signed.

British officials say the Bosnian Moslems, Serbs and Croats are violating Dayton by hampering freedom of movement, preventing refugees from returning home, committing human rights abuses and refusing to hand over indicted war criminals.

International mediator Carl Bildt said on Wednesday new methods may be used to bring indicted war criminals before the Hague tribunal if the former warring factions persist in refusing to hand them over for trial.
